physics_goals.quote: uses the parity violating weak neutral interaction to probe the neutron distribution in a heavy nucleus, namely 208Pb
physics_goals.value: Measure the neutron distribution radius of 208Pb (the neutron skin) via parity-violating electron scattering to about 1%

summary.plain: PREX used spinning electron beams on lead to measure the neutron skin of lead-208, how far its neutrons extend beyond its protons. The first run (2010) and the second (PREX-II, 2019) showed a thick skin that matters for the structure of neutron stars.
summary.technical: Lead Radius Experiment (E12-11-101 for PREX-II) in Hall A: parity-violating elastic scattering of longitudinally polarised ~950 MeV electrons from 208Pb at Q^2 ~ 0.006 GeV^2, measuring the neutral weak form factor and hence the neutron radius. PREX-I (2010) gave the first electroweak observation of the neutron skin; PREX-II (2019) combined result R_n - R_p = 0.283 ± 0.071 fm.
